cases.title: Closeout records independently observed public facts without changing unrelated evidence
cases.risk: Closeout fabricates public success, accepts inconsistent observations or overwrites evidence outside the selected release.

conditions: Use publication with controlled GitHub/npm/smoke facts and snapshots of pending, earlier-release and unrelated files. Vary provider values independently of the generated expectations.
Use explicit fixture mode only for fixture evidence; historical-reader is a separate immutable input and cannot qualify a current routine profile.

when: Run real closeout and the documented public version/target smoke commands.
Repeat with unavailable facts, failed smoke, wrong serialized command/hash scope or a missing target; establish a successful baseline before corrupting evidence.
Invoke closeout check mode and inspect the filesystem.
then: Successful evidence records observed version, intended tag/integrity, asset hashes and both target smoke results; it never substitutes prepared expectations.
Unavailable facts or failed smoke preserve pending/unrelated bytes and report the failure. Invalid serialized evidence rejects; earlier evidence stays byte-identical.
Fixture evidence requires explicit mode at function and CLI boundaries. Check mode reports planned output without finalizing it.
The admitted historical reader does not admit its old target population as a new routine profile.

gaps: Closeout check mode reports planned output without finalizing it: The existing case checks the report; add a byte snapshot of all release and unrelated files to establish the complete no-write promise.

Published evidence rejects wrong command, hash scope and missing target: Add an explicit no-error assertion on the valid baseline within each negative case before mutation; the current negative methods rely on the shared successful fixture.
Automated realization removed under the maintainer-selected minimal suite. This scenario is not claimed covered by the retained suite; see design/support/validation.md.

cases.title: Release evidence distinguishes passed, failed and explicitly deferred duties
cases.risk: A checklist labels failed, unobserved or unauthorized deferred work as successful release proof.

conditions: Use checklist for ordinary published evidence and emergency only for a separately authorized exception. Start from valid evidence, then mutate a required row/result or exception field independently.

when: Validate the real checklist in each state, including missing/duplicate rows, unknown result/status, forbidden pending results, secret-bearing text and incomplete/forbidden emergency deferral.
then: Complete applicable evidence passes; failed required gates block and no absent/duplicate/unknown row silently passes.
A permitted deferred duty has exactly one matching record with owner, authority, rationale, impact, risk, follow-up and deadline; registry identity and other nondeferrable duties remain required.
Secrets reject. A structurally valid exception establishes representation only, never the owner approval assessed by REL-MR-002.

cases.title: Timing stays truthful diagnostic data and cannot mask release correctness
cases.risk: Optional observability becomes a false release gate or its tolerance weakens required correctness.

conditions: Use timing for document checks and execution for the actual publication consequence. Keep release identity/profile valid while timing is absent, pending, malformed or above its advisory duration target; separately invalidate the profile.

when: Validate timing representation and run actual execution with controlled providers.
then: Emitted timing reports measured versus pending/unavailable data honestly; missing fields and unknown values produce their diagnostic errors.
Absent/malformed/slow timing alone does not suppress otherwise successful publication. No missing duration is invented.
A malformed release profile still blocks; diagnostic tolerance cannot waive identity or check failures.
